content.text:
### Run Chromium in Single-Process Mode

Source: https://www.chromium.org/developers/how-tos/debugging-on-windows

Add this command-line flag to run Chromium in single-process mode for easier debugging. Note that some issues may not manifest in this mode.

```shell
--single-process
```

### Multi-process Architecture

Source: https://www.chromium.org/developers/design-documents/multi-process-architecture

Chromium's multi-process architecture aims to provide robustness and security by isolating web content rendering into separate processes. This design prevents a single misbehaving web page or plugin from crashing the entire browser, similar to how modern operating systems isolate applications.

--------------------------------

### Inter-process Communication (IPC) > Overview

Source: https://www.chromium.org/developers/design-documents/inter-process-communication

Chromium employs a multi-process architecture where various processes communicate using named pipes as the primary inter-process communication (IPC) primitive. On Linux and OS X, socket pairs are utilized. Each renderer process is allocated a named pipe for communication with the browser process, and these pipes operate in asynchronous mode to prevent blocking.

--------------------------------

### Multi-process Resource Loading > Background

Source: https://www.chromium.org/developers/design-documents/multi-process-resource-loading

In Chromium's multi-process architecture, the main browser process manages all network communication. This central control ensures that the browser process can regulate network access for each renderer, maintain consistent session state (like cookies and cached data) across all processes, and adhere to connection limits per host as an HTTP/1.1 user-agent.

--------------------------------

### Architecture Overview > Frame Representation > Proxies

Source: https://www.chromium.org/developers/design-documents/oop-iframes

To enable cross-process communication like postMessage, Chromium maintains proxy DOMWindows in renderer processes for all reachable frames. These proxies allow a document in one process to route messages to a document in another process via the browser, without requiring a full document or V8 context for the proxy itself.
